context.title: Into Europe: Philippi
context.summary: Timothy joins Paul and Silas. A vision calls them to Macedonia. In Philippi Lydia believes, a slave girl is freed from a spirit, Paul and Silas are beaten and jailed, and an earthquake leads to the jailer's conversion.
context.background: Philippi was a Roman colony, settled by retired soldiers and governed by Roman law. In v. 10 the narration switches to 'we', suggesting the author joined the journey. The first meeting is by a river 'where prayer was wont to be made' (v. 13), perhaps because there was no synagogue.

customs.note: Purple cloth was costly. Lydia came from Thyatira, a city known for dyeing, and headed her own household.
Roman law forbade beating a Roman citizen without a trial. The magistrates had broken it, which is why they become afraid.

watchFor: Paul and Silas sing hymns at midnight in the stocks (v. 25).
'Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house' (v. 31).

people.name: Timotheus
people.summary: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5).

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Lydia
people.summary: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13).

people.name: Silas
people.summary: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus. He and Judas, surnamed Barsabas, were chosen by the church there to accompany Paul and Barnabas on their return to Antioch from the council of the apostles and elders (Acts 15:22), as bearers of the decree adopted by the council.

places.name: Derbe
places.summary: A small town on the eastern part of the upland plain of Lycaonia, about 20 miles from Lystra. Paul passed through Derbe on his route from Cilicia to Iconium, on his second missionary journey (Acts 16:1), and probably also on his third journey (18:23; 19:1).

places.name: Lystra
places.summary: A town of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor, in a wild district and among a rude population. Here Paul preached the gospel after he had been driven by persecution from Iconium (Acts 14:2-7).

places.name: Iconium
places.summary: The capital of ancient Lycaonia. It was first visited by Paul and Barnabas from Antioch-in-Pisidia during the apostle’s first missionary journey (Acts 13:50, 51).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Asia
places.summary: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2.

places.name: Galatia
places.summary: Has been called the “Gallia” of the East, Roman writers calling its inhabitants Galli. They were an intermixture of Gauls and Greeks, and hence were called Gallo-Graeci, and the country Gallo-Graecia.

places.name: Phrygia
places.summary: Dry, an irregular and ill-defined district in Asia Minor. It was divided into two parts, the Greater Phrygia on the south, and the Lesser Phrygia on the west.

places.name: Bithynia
places.summary: A province in Asia Minor, to the south of the Euxine and Propontis. Christian congregations were here formed at an early time (1 Pet. 1:1). Paul was prevented by the Spirit from entering this province (Acts 16:7).

places.name: Mysia
places.summary: A province in the north-west of Asia Minor.

places.name: Troas
places.summary: A city on the coast of Mysia, in the north-west of Asia Minor, named after ancient Troy, which was at some little distance from it (about 4 miles) to the north.

places.name: Macedonia
places.summary: In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul. Paul was summoned by the vision of the “man of Macedonia” to preach the gospel there (Acts 16:9).

places.name: Neapolis
places.summary: New city, a town in Thrace at which Paul first landed in Europe (Acts 16:11). It was the sea-port of the inland town of Philippi, which was distant about 10 miles.

places.name: Samothrace
places.summary: An island in the AEgean Sea, off the coast of Thracia, about 32 miles distant. This Thracian Samos was passed by Paul on his voyage from Troas to Neapolis (Acts 16:11) on his first missionary journey.

places.name: Philippi
places.summary: Formerly Crenides, “the fountain,” the capital of the province of Macedonia. It stood near the head of the Sea, about 8 miles north-west of Kavalla.

places.name: Thyatira
places.summary: A city of Asia Minor, on the borders of Lydia and Mysia. Its modern name is Ak-hissar, i.e., “white castle.” Here was one of the seven churches (Rev. 1:11; 2:18-28).

events.title: Second Missionary Journey
events.summary: Passage: Acts 15:1–18:23. People: Simon, Paul, Luke, Silas, Barnabas, Timotheus and others. Lasted about 3 years.

events.title: Timothy Joins Paul and Silas
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:1–5. People: Paul, Timotheus, Silas. Place: Lystra, Derbe. Lasted about 1 month.

events.title: Mission to Phrygia, Galatia and Asia
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:6–8. People: Timotheus, Paul, Silas, Holy Spirit. Place: Troas, Mysia, Asia, Galatia. Lasted about 1 month.

events.title: Call to Macedonia
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:9–12. People: Paul, Timotheus, Silas, Luke. Place: Philippi, Neapolis, Samothrace, Troas. Lasted about 4 months.

events.title: Lydia's Conversion
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:13–15. People: Paul, Lydia, Timotheus, Silas, Luke. Place: Philippi.

events.title: Paul casts demon out of soothsayer
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:16–18. People: Paul, Timotheus, Silas, Luke. Place: Philippi.

events.title: Paul and Silas imprisoned
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:19–34. People: Silas, Paul. Place: Philippi.

events.title: Philippian jailer converted
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:25–34. People: Silas, Paul. Place: Philippi.

events.title: Paul and Silas released
events.summary: Passage: Acts 16:35–40. People: Lydia, Paul, Silas. Place: Philippi.
